result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B sets a clear outcome for the call and checks for it with gate criteria. Its questions are open-ended and specific to refrigeration, and it tells the seller to get the cost of a failure from her rather than suggest one. It ends with a dated next step that names who should attend. A is solid and practical, but its goal is softer, several of its questions can be answered yes or no, and it never explicitly says to let her put the number on failure cost. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A says exactly what has to be true by the end of the call: a problem she can put a size on, a signer or a way to reach one, and something she'll commit to. It also tells you to get the failure cost from her, never suggest a number, and end on a dated call with the decision-maker. B has good ramen-specific detail (stocks, tare, a central prep kitchen) and good objection handling, but its goal is looser, several questions can be answered yes or no, and it leans on the seller framing the cost (one emergency call plus lost inventory) instead of drawing the number out of her.
